outcome: time from patient admission to onset of labor
inpatient stay from admission to delivery
cohort: The study included 96 low-risk patients receiving outpatient mechanical cervical ripening, 99 patients receiving inpatient oral misoprostol, and 42 patients receiving inpatient vaginal dinoprostone for labor induction.
finding: Outpatient mechanical cervical ripening was found to be as safe and effective as inpatient cervical ripening with misoprostol or dinoprostone, while significantly lowering patient-staff contact, total hospital stays, and socioeconomic costs.
mod_finding: Delivery modes were similar across all groups of cervical ripening methods.
